Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-e83c0c27: template occurrences in binary noise

## Reusable rule

The input is mostly two-color noise (here 0 and 8) plus a small seed object in another color. Treat the seed object’s colored cells as a fixed-orientation shape mask within its bounding box. Scan every possible translation of that mask across the grid. A placement matches when every input cell at a mask position is 0; ignore the values in the bounding-box holes. Recolor the union of the matched mask cells to the seed object's color. Preserve all nonmatching cells, including the original seed. Do not rotate or reflect the template unless a demonstration proves that is allowed.

## Evidence from this instance

Demo 1 has a color-1 L seed at zero-indexed coordinates `(6,2),(6,3),(7,2)`, i.e. mask `[(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)]`. Matching every translation whose three mask cells are 0 and recoloring their union to 1 reproduces the demo output exactly (80 changed cells; no extras or misses). This validates that the unused corner of its 2x2 bounding box is ignored.

The test has a color-7 template with a 4x3 bounding box. Relative to its top-left `(7,13)`, mask coordinates are `[(0,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2),(3,0),(3,1),(3,2)]`. Exactly one all-zero match occurs at top-left `(11,8)`. Recolor those eight cells to 7 and leave everything else untouched; this was accepted as correct.

Correctly recolored test cells (zero-indexed): `(11,8),(12,9),(12,10),(13,9),(13,10),(14,8),(14,9),(14,10)`.

## Pitfalls learned

- Carefully transcribe the seed's exact occupied coordinates. A prior incorrect attempt omitted `(0,0)` and mistakenly used `(0,2)` in the 4x3 mask, painting seven of the eight matched cells and missing `(11,8)`.
- The pattern is not just an L triomino for the test: use all occupied seed pixels, preserving its fixed orientation.
- Don't recolor all zero matches of some simpler sub-shape; overlapping sub-shapes produce many false positives.
- Keep the seed's original colored cells unchanged; paint only zeros in matching placements.

## task-3475df40: mark the difference between repeated horizontal bars

Evidence from two demos and the accepted test solution:

- Find matching/repeated horizontal bars (same background plus one foreground color), where one bar is shorter and the corresponding comparison bar reaches farther.
- On the shorter bar only, recolor its contiguous trailing background cells to color `1` to mark the continuation/difference. Keep foreground cells, leading background, and other rows unchanged.
- Demo 1: background 6, bar color 7; row with 7s through column 24 was the reference, and another row with 7s through column 17 had columns 18–24 changed from 6 to 1.
- Demo 2: background 5, bar color 0; full row of 0s was the reference, and partial row with 0s through column 15 had columns 16–17 changed from 5 to 1.
- Accepted test: background 2, bar color 7; in the repeated two-row motifs, the lower second bar ended at column 10 while the matching upper bar continued to column 14. Only lower row columns 11–14 were changed from 2 to 1. The similar lower first row and upper second row were left unchanged.

Avoid marking every short-looking line: compare the repeated motif/bar rows, and mark only the trailing difference for the shorter counterpart. The first submission was wrong because it marked row 2 and row 13; the corrected submission marked only row 14, columns 11–14, and was accepted.

### Additional accepted instance (2026-09-29)

A separate instance carrying this task id had background 6 and foreground 8, with two similar 6-row motifs. In the lower motif, row 21 (0-based) had foreground through column 6 while its counterpart row 8 was foreground through column 11; likewise row 23 ended at column 6 while counterpart row 10 extended through column 11. The accepted output changed only columns 7–11 of rows 21 and 23 to color 1. All other cells remained unchanged. This supports comparing corresponding rows across repeated motifs and marking only the shorter motif's missing trailing segment; do not fill ordinary short rows unless their matching motif counterpart is longer.

# Continual-ARC notes

## Hollow-frame fill by interior parity

Evidence from task `task-e745fcf4` (solved): preserve the background and outline, and fill the enclosed interior of each hollow rectangular/square frame based on the interior side length parity:

- Even-by-even interior dimensions -> fill with color 2.
- Odd-by-odd interior dimensions -> fill with color 7.

Observed examples: 6x6 and 2x2 interiors became 2; 5x5, 3x3, and 1x1 interiors became 7. This applied regardless of outline color (seen with colors 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9). In the test grid, the 5x5 outer frames had 3x3 interiors -> 7; the 4x4 outer frame had 2x2 interior -> 2; the 3x3 frame had 1x1 interior -> 7.

Practical procedure: identify each closed, one-cell-thick frame; inspect dimensions of the enclosed interior (not the outer frame); fill only the interior uniformly with 2 for even side lengths and 7 for odd side lengths. Leave all other cells unchanged. The task's tested objects were square frames.
